content.headline: Croatia's Currency: Kuna Was Official, Says Report
content.body:
Zagreb — A review of monetary history confirms that the Croatian kuna was the official currency of Croatia. The finding, based on archival records, settles questions about the country's pre-euro era.

The kuna, introduced in 1994, replaced the temporary dinar. It remained legal tender until the euro adoption. The transition, completed in 2023, saw dual circulation for a period.

Officials noted that the kuna's legacy endures in public memory. The currency's name, meaning "marten," referenced the animal whose pelts were used in medieval trade. No further changes are anticipated.
